description: The token sets SPEC.md names and expects an implementation to spell identically, published as data so a spelling can be generated or checked rather than transcribed. A derived view: the specification governs, this file restates no requirement's substance, and a disagreement is a bug here.

spec_refs: SPEC.md Section 10.4 "Emitted Runtime Events (Upstream to Orchestrator)"
events.note: The neutral event vocabulary every adapter MUST emit (Section 10.7). Not a closed set: Section 10.4 states that an adapter MAY emit additional events and that a consumer MUST tolerate an unrecognized name, so a generated type MUST admit an unknown token rather than closing the enum. The names are fixed for the conditions they do name.

spec_refs: SPEC.md Section 10.4 "Emitted Runtime Events (Upstream to Orchestrator)"
event_envelope_fields.note: What each emitted event SHOULD include. Payload fields beyond these are event-specific.

entries.note: The neutral token-usage record (`token_usage_fields`), with any adapter-specific counts in an opaque extras field.

log_context_fields.note: REQUIRED log context, by what the log is about. Section 18.1.1 makes structured logs carrying all three a conformance item for every implementation.

spec_refs: SPEC.md Section 13.5 "Session Metrics and Token Accounting"
token_usage_fields.note: The neutral token-usage record each adapter normalizes its protocol's usage payloads into. Absolute cumulative totals, never deltas (Section 13.5); adapter-specific counts such as cache tokens go in an extras field rather than here.

ledger_entry_fields.note: One entry of the OPTIONAL per-execution usage ledger: a full absolute snapshot of one session's token usage at one observation. Entries are keyed by (`issue_identifier`, `session_id`); `required: true` marks a field whose absence makes the entry invalid and MUST be skipped on read.

recovery_classes.note: Every Orchestrator Runtime State field (Section 4.1.8), and any state an OPTIONAL extension introduces, MUST be assigned exactly one class, published in the Conformance Statement (Section 19).

runtime_state_fields.note: The single authoritative runtime state and the recovery class Section 4.1.8 states for each field. An implementation records its own assignment in its Conformance Statement (Section 19); this is the specification's, which is what that record is compared against.

entries.note: Becomes `Durable` when a budgeting extension enforces on it, and is then Symphony-attributed rather than account-wide.
An absent value denotes `UNKNOWN`, distinct from any reading and in particular not `0`.

spec_refs: SPEC.md Section 18.2 "RECOMMENDED Extensions (Not REQUIRED for Conformance)"
config_namespaces.note: Top-level configuration keys and the artifact each belongs to (Section 5). `core: true` marks a key the core schema defines; the rest are owned by the OPTIONAL extension named in `spec_ref`, and an implementation publishes the namespaces it ships in its Conformance Statement (Section 19). Not a closed set: Section 5.3 permits an extension to define additional top-level keys.

entries.note: Its `transitions` field is repository-owned and lives in `repo.policy.toml` (Section 11.6).
In-sandbox hooks in `WORKFLOW.md`, host-side hooks in `repo.policy.toml` (Section 15.4).
Reserved for observability settings (Section 13); the specification names the namespace, not the fields. Ledger settings are `observability.ledger.*` (Section 13.6).
Section 13.8 starts the HTTP server when a CLI `--port` argument is given or `server.port` is present in `WORKFLOW.md` front matter.

spec_refs: SPEC.md Section 5.5 "Workflow Validation and Error Surface"
SPEC.md Section 5.1 "WORKFLOW.md Discovery and Path Resolution"
error_classes.note: The classes the workflow loader and the prompt renderer fail with. A class names the condition, not the stage at which an implementation detects it: an unknown variable and an unknown filter are both `template_render_error` however early the template engine resolves them, and `template_parse_error` is reserved for a body that is not well-formed template syntax at all. `gating` is Section 5.5's dispatch gating behavior, which is the part a consumer acts on (Sections 6.2, 12.4): `blocks_dispatch` holds new dispatches until the file is repaired, `fails_attempt` fails only the affected run attempt. Not a closed set: Section 5.5 permits an implementation to define additional classes for conditions these five do not name, and requires it to document each one and assign it a gating behavior.

entries.condition: The workflow file cannot be read at the resolved path (Section 5.1).
The YAML front matter is not well-formed (Section 5.2).
The front matter is well-formed YAML that does not decode to a map (Section 5.2).
The prompt body is not well-formed template syntax.
The body is well formed and names something the engine cannot resolve: an unknown variable, an unknown filter, or an invalid interpolation (Section 5.4).

tracker_error_categories.note: Transport-neutral categories each tracker adapter maps its transport's failures onto. RECOMMENDED, so the names are a target vocabulary rather than a checked spelling; a generated type MUST admit an unknown token. The first three entries carry no `condition` because Section 11.4 states none. Section 17.3 requires four of them by name in `Core Conformance` checks — `tracker_unsupported_operation`, `tracker_state_unreachable`, `tracker_state_conflict`, `tracker_pagination_error` — which is a disagreement with this level recorded in `conformance/README.md` rather than resolved here.

entries.condition: Write not in the adapter capability descriptor (Section 11.7).
`set_state` target unreachable from the current state (Section 11.8).
Issue state changed underneath a `set_state` write (Section 11.8).
Unsuccessful response status, for example non-2xx HTTP.
Backend-reported errors in a well-formed response, for example a GraphQL `errors` array.
Pagination integrity failure, for example a missing continuation cursor.

agent_error_categories.note: Normalized categories an agent adapter maps its protocol's failures onto. RECOMMENDED, so the names are a target vocabulary rather than a checked spelling; a generated type MUST admit an unknown token. Section 10.6 states no condition for any of them. `turn_failed`, `turn_cancelled` and `turn_input_required` are also `events` entries (Section 10.4): the category is named after the event that produced it, so a generator emitting one type per group has three names in two enums by design rather than by collision.
